study.question: baseline-din achieves macro AUC 0.8099233881 and macro Logloss 0.05662295138; click/cart/fav/buy AUCs are 0.65554408/0.84906970/0.86489749/0.87018228. Its code collapses all visible histories into one target-conditioned vector with action embeddings only in values, then shares that vector across task towers. Empty, 1-16, 17-64 and >64 history macro AUCs are 0.72684289, 0.76284093, 0.78929094 and 0.82734437. These observational slices have different prevalences and do not identify a bottleneck. Does retaining feedback-conditioned content as distinct units improve field/history joint modeling beyond identical token capacity, explicit feedback counts, or generic recency partitioning?
study.hypothesis: A single summed vector can entangle which item-field evidence accompanies each historical feedback type. Global plus four overlapping behavior summaries may preserve this conditional content for interaction with user/context/target fields and all prediction heads. The decisive comparison is behavior content versus count-proportional global content with exactly the same semantic counts/occupancy. This is a testable local hypothesis, not an established limitation or verified novelty claim.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary DIN text, lines 268-277, supports target-conditioned unnormalized local activation. Inherit the supplied field/task adaptation, not its paper training recipe. Add separately addressable history summaries and field/summary attention; the shared network never receives current action or labels.

Pinned primary benchmark source lines 112-158 pools all history before global/chunk field tokenization and reversible mixing. Here retain feedback-specific content before compression into five slots and use one ordinary masked attention block, not that mixing operator. Original TokenMixer paper was only link-resolved, not audited; priority is unverified.

Pinned source lines 129-237 uses recent/earlier event partitions with fixed and feature-conditioned queries. The candidate instead groups by released feedback masks under one shared DIN scorer; recency_slots is a rank-quartile replacement control, not a HeMix reproduction. Original-method originality remains unverified.

Pinned source lines 117-190 keeps fields, each history event and target in a token sequence. This study uses field tokens and five compact history slots; it does not run full/sliding event attention or claim equivalent modeling capacity.

Cached primary benchmark section 2.3 confirms that pooling plus token mixing, multiple summaries, and unified token interaction are existing architectural ingredients. This proposal tests a local representation contrast and makes no claim to a new architectural family.

Only the author README was available, warning that its behavior data lacks item identity. It does not establish transfer to these previous advertisement IDs. No DMR mechanism or exact reproduction claim is inherited.

study.proposed_difference: Implement a field-plus-five-slot representation with shared DIN scores and shared slot projection. Slots are all exposure, historical click, cart, favorite and purchase; action types can overlap. A slot contains an unnormalized group sum over item/action embeddings plus a normalized log count. One 32-wide two-head masked attention block jointly interacts with individual static field tokens. The readout retains original raw static fields and global DIN sum, flattened interacted tokens, and counts. Four standalone modules have identical trainable tensors and differ only in slot_mode. Counts control replaces group content with count-proportional global content; pooled control repeats the global vector/count; recency control uses ordinal quartiles. No network/filesystem operations, extra data, timestamps, label hooks or host-contract changes are introduced. All stronger originality and mechanism claims await evidence.
predictions: If conditional content preservation matters, behavior_slots will improve full-validation macro AUC over count_scaled_slots, with trade-offs reported for all four tasks and macro Logloss. No task-specific veto is added.

If semantic grouping is more useful than generic multi-summary capacity here, behavior_slots will also exceed recency_slots and pooled_slots. A gain only against baseline-din is insufficient mechanism evidence.

Behavior effects should primarily concern nonempty histories with feedback support. Analyze the existing fixed length bins, reporting sample/positive/negative counts and marking small slices; additional behavior-composition bins are exploratory unless fixed using training data before execution. No gain is predicted from unavailable raw timestamps.

All four variants have exactly equal parameter tensors/shapes at the same feature map and config. They have the same dominant DIN scoring cost but possibly different masking/grouping runtime. Dense parameters exceed DIN due to projections/attention/readout; equal training recipe does not imply equal compute.

Host preflight must show finite four-task [B,1] probabilities and gradients on mixed/empty/single-event histories; invariance to masked ID/action/multi-mask perturbations in evaluation and train mode with reset RNG/state; invariance to target action; and correct overlap/absence/recency mask semantics. These checks are pending, not reported as passed.
falsifiers: Across budget-permitted paired repeats, behavior_slots fails to outperform the same-count count_scaled_slots; this weakens the useful conditional-content explanation for this implementation, even if both beat DIN.
Recency or replicated global slots match or outperform behavior slots; semantic feedback grouping is not established as the preferred representation.
Only count_scaled_slots improves, or all four improve similarly over DIN; counts or the common interaction/readout scaffold are viable explanations and grouping attribution is unsupported.
A score depends on masked IDs/actions, current target action, current labels, or unexposed information; reject that implementation before predictive interpretation.
A variant exceeds the frozen 1208.541376-second cap, fails finite-output/gradient checks, or cannot fit host resources; record execution failure and charged cost, not a negative scientific result.
alternative_explanations: Observed baseline slice differences can arise from prevalence, user composition and training frequency rather than representation loss.
Explicit counts/occupancy may explain a gain; count_scaled_slots controls them while keeping global content and count-proportional scale.

Any improvement over DIN can arise from common dense capacity, attention, optimization or retained readout paths. The four new variants isolate representations conditional on that scaffold, not interaction itself.
Overlapping behavioral groups duplicate exposures; recency groups are disjoint. Differences in support, scale, sparsity and overlap remain relevant even with matched parameter count.

Shared Dice scoring retains batch-coupled statistics, although padded inputs are sanitized. One-pass convergence or changed gradient routing may favor a representation without showing intrinsic information superiority.

Released offline feedback can include delayed outcomes not mature at impression time. Auxiliary labels match user/category/brand within 24h and are not ad-specific conversion attribution. Results would establish this benchmark only.

Only one baseline trajectory is authorized, with no earlier failed/abandoned local research branches or candidate outcomes. No multiple-trajectory/repeated-support conclusion is currently possible; retain all future receipts, including failures.
